places.name: San Antonio
places.note: Call and Gus buy a wagon and mules north of the river; at the Buckhorn saloon Gus bloodies a rude bartender, sheriff Tobe vouches for them, and they leave past the neglected Alamo.

places.name: Settlements south of San Antonio
places.note: Two tiny new hamlets with a church and a few stores prompt Augustus to complain that settlement is ruining the country.
places.location_hint: on the ride from the herd into San Antonio, under ten miles apart, south of the city

places.name: Tennessee
places.note: Augustus says had he wanted civilization he would have stayed there writing poetry.

places.name: New Orleans
places.note: Augustus jokes San Antonio may rival it if it keeps growing.

places.name: Fort Worth
places.note: Former Buckhorn owner Willie Montgomery now lives there with the woman he chased.

places.name: Canadian River
places.note: The Rangers once chased Kicking Wolf's band all the way to it, earning brief fame and a photograph.

places.name: Brazos River
places.note: Kicking Wolf had raided settlers down along it before the Rangers drove him off.

places.name: Mobile
places.note: Hometown of John, the hot-tempered new Buckhorn owner.

places.name: Montana
places.note: Tobe wistfully says he might have joined the drive there if not married.

places.name: Washington, D.C.
places.note: Call scoffs that a thousand Comanches together could have taken it.

places.name: Texas
places.note: When they first came in the Forties, everyone still talked of Travis and the Alamo.

groups.label: Call and Augustus
groups.hint: leaving town at night with a new wagon, heading back to the herd

groups.label: Hat Creek outfit
groups.hint: with the herd south of San Antonio, waiting for a new wagon
